t.p: mid-18th century to present (records from the Keichō era)
t.d: Hand-made lanterns of thin Mino washi over a fine bamboo frame, a designated Japanese traditional craft since 1995; the source of Noguchi's Akari.
t.tech: bamboo strips wound on a mould, paper pasted (hari), designs stencilled or painted (surikomi), wooden parts finished (moriage); work split among specialists
t.mat: Mino washi or silk, madake or hachiku bamboo, cedar, cypress or magnolia wood
t.auth: double-layered upper ring hiding the shade joint; regional brandmark since 2006

t.d: Lamp shades of cut coloured glass wrapped in copper foil and soldered over a mould, developed at Tiffany Studios.
t.tech: watercolour design, paper patterns and numbered templates, glass cut and copper-foiled, soldered on a wooden mould
t.mat: opalescent and coloured glass, copper foil, solder, bronze bases
t.auth: copper-foil construction and Tiffany Studios attribution; most 'Tiffany lamps' are later Tiffany-style copies

t.p: glassmaking confined to Murano from 1291; peak 15th–16th c.; revivals after 1866 and in the 1920s
t.d: Venetian hot-worked soda glass, including chandeliers of hand-shaped flowers and leaves.
t.tech: hot-working, filigrana, murrine, sommerso, gilding and enamel
t.auth: 'Artistic Glass Murano' trademark (1994) certifies Murano manufacture; Asian and Eastern European imitations are common.

t.p: from c. 1250; high Baroque fame 1685–1750; chandelier industry from 1724
t.d: Clear potash and lead crystal, cut and engraved, including the Maria Theresa and crystal chandelier.
t.tech: hand-cutting, wheel engraving, blowing, enamel painting
t.auth: EU 'lead crystal' needs at least 24% lead oxide; lower-lead pieces are 'crystal glass'.

t.p: Recorded from 1085; regional forms flourished in the Edo period
t.d: Collapsible paper lanterns of washi stretched over a spiral split-bamboo frame that folds into its base.
t.tech: Paper attached to the frame (hari), designs added (surikomi), powder on exposed wood (moriage); work often split between specialists
t.mat: Washi (Mino, Nishinouchi), split bamboo, wood, copper or brass fittings
t.auth: Gifu lanterns: designated traditional craft (1995) with a regional brandmark (2006); hand-applied washi on bamboo, not printed fabric or plastic

t.p: Most prominent in the Ottoman era; made today
t.d: Lamps whose blown-glass shades are covered in small hand-cut pieces of coloured glass.
t.tech: Glass pieces glued by hand onto a clear blown globe, gaps filled with paste, shade fitted to a metal frame
t.mat: Coloured glass, clear blown glass, beads, brass or bronze
t.auth: Slight variation between pieces, deep colour when lit, heavy bronze base, glass rings when tapped (plastic copies sound dull)

t.d: Brass lanterns cut or punched with geometric and floral openwork, often glazed with coloured glass.
t.tech: Sheet brass pierced, hammered, chased and worked in repoussé; glass panes set in
t.mat: Brass, coloured, seeded or etched glass
t.auth: Many 'Moroccan-style' lanterns are made elsewhere (notably India); check origin and hand-cut rather than stamped work
